content.heading: Negligence
content.text: A person is liable in negligence when they owe the claimant a duty of care, breach that duty by failing to take the care a reasonable person would take in the circumstances, and thereby cause damage to the claimant that is not too remote. Duty is informed by foresight of harm to persons so closely and directly affected that they ought reasonably to be in contemplation. Breach is judged objectively. Causation requires that the breach was a necessary cause of the loss and that the kind of damage was reasonably foreseeable. Contributory negligence and volenti may reduce or defeat recovery as defences.
